safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) the wāw of the oath, putting the noun in the genitive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم "I swear"; (صفّا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its governor being الصافّات; (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (زجرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, its governor being الزاجرات; (ذكرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its synonym [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) if الذكر is the Qur'an.]; (اللام) the lām of the oath, in compensation for the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).
The clause « (أقسم) بالصافّات..» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «إنّ إلهكم لواحد ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(الصافّات): plural of الصّافّة, the feminine of الصافّ, an active participle of the verb صفّ of the نصر class; its pattern is فاعل, its ʿayn and lām being of one letter. Its masculine plural is صافّون, صافّين.. and the feminine plural is صوافّ on the pattern فواعل [Note: See verse (36) of Sūrat al-Ḥajj.]. (الزاجرات): plural of الزاجرة, the feminine of الزاجر, an active participle of the three-letter verb زجر of the نصر class; its pattern is فاعل; its masculine plural is الزاجرون, الزاجرين.. and the feminine زواجر.
(زجرا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) known by hearsay (samāʿī) of the verb زجر; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(التاليات): plural of التالية, the feminine of التالي, an active participle of the three-letter verb تلا of the نصر class; its pattern is فاعل. It contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb): its original form is التالو with kasra on the lām; the wāw was changed into a yāʾ because the letter before it has kasra. Its masculine plural is التالون, التالين, and in both there is a weak-letter change by omission because of the meeting of two quiescent letters: the original form is التاليون, التاليين; the ḍamma and the kasra on the yāʾ were felt heavy, so they were transferred to the two letters before them, and when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ, the lām of the word, was omitted; its pattern is فاعون, فاعين.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) a badal (substitute) of واحد, nominative [Note: Or it is a second khabar (predicate) of the particle resembling the verb, or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هو, and the clause is resumptive.]; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a relative in the position of genitive, conjoined to السموات; (بينهما) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (الواو) conjunction; (ربّ) conjoined to the first ربّ, nominative like it.

safi-cedvel:6-10.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (بزينة) attached to (زيّنا); (الكواكب) a badal (substitute) of زينة — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it — genitive.
The clause «إنّا زيّنا..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «زيّنا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
(7) (حفظا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; (من كلّ) attached to the omitted verb..
The clause « (حفظناها) حفظا» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause زيّنا..
(8) (لا) negating; (إلى الملأ) attached to (يسّمّعون), by making it include the meaning of يصغون "they listen attentively"; (الواو) conjunction, and (الواو) in (يقذفون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (من كلّ) attached to (يقذفون).
The clause «لا يسّمّعون..» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: It is not valid for the clause to be a naʿt (adjective) of (كلّ شيطان), since it would then be described as not listening or not hearing, which is unsound; nor is it valid for it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), though al-ʿUkbarī permitted both.].
The clause «يقذفون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لا يسّمّعون.
(9) (دحورا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its synonym [Note: Or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl.]; (الواو) conjunction; (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) عذاب..
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لا يسّمّعون.
(10) (إلّا) for exception; (من) a relative in the position of nominative as a badal of the agent of يسّمّعون [Note: Or in the position of accusative as excepted.]; (الخطفة) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative; (الفاء) conjunction.
The clause «خطف» .. has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «أتبعه شهاب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خطف ...

* Morphology:
(7) مارد: an active participle of the three-letter verb مرد of the كرم class; its pattern is فاعل, and it means "insolent, rebellious".
(9) دحورا: maṣdar (verbal noun) of دحر of the فتح class; its pattern is فعول with two ḍammas.
(10) الخطفة: a maṣdar of once-ness (maṣdar marra) from the three-letter verb خطف of the فرح class; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.
(ثاقب): an active participle of the three-letter verb ثقب; its pattern is فاعل.

* Benefits:
His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِزِينَةٍ الْكَواكِبِ. وَحِفْظاً مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطانٍ مارِدٍ. لا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ الْأَعْلى. وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِنْ كُلِّ جانِبٍ — Ibn Hishām said, concerning the i'rab of the clause (لا يسّمعون): What first comes to mind is that it is an adjective (of لكل شيطان), or a ḥāl of it, and both are false, since there is no sense in guarding against a devil that does not hear. Rather it is for grammatical resumption (istiʾnāf naḥwī), and it cannot be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) because of the corruption of meaning. It has been said: it is possible that the original was «لئلا يسمعوا» "so that they would not hear", then the لام was omitted, as in your saying «جئتك أن تكرمني» "I came to you that you might honour me", then «أن» was omitted and the verb became nominative, as in the saying of Ṭarafa:
ألا أيّهذا الزاجري أحضر الوغى ... وأن أشهد اللذات هل أنت مخلدي
(O you who chide me for attending the battle and for witnessing pleasures — will you make me immortal?)
according to those who read أحضر in the nominative. But al-Zamakhsharī considered weak the combination of the two omissions (i.e. the omission of the لام and of أن). If you say: "I make it an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), i.e. 'and as a guard against every rebellious devil, its not hearing being anticipated', i.e. after the guarding", I say: the one who anticipates the existence of the meaning of the ḥāl is the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl), like the one passed by in your saying «مررت به معه صقر صائدا به غدا» "I passed by him with a falcon, hunting with it tomorrow", i.e. anticipating, at the time of being passed by, that he will hunt with it tomorrow; and the devils do not anticipate not hearing, nor do they want it.
After the Imam al-Nasafī cited the words of Ibn Hishām, he said:
In these words there is a forcedness from which the Qur'an must be protected. For each of the two particles (i.e. the لام and أن) is not rejected on its own, but their combination is objectionable. Then he mentioned the difference between our saying سمعت فلانا يتحدث "I heard so-and-so speaking" and سمعت إليه يتحدث "I listened to him speaking", or سمعت حديثه "I heard his speech" and سمعت إلى حديثه "I listened to his speech", and he said: the verb that is transitive by itself conveys perception, and the one that is transitive by إلى conveys listening attentively along with perception.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (خلقا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (أم) a conjunction; (من) a relative in the position of nominative, conjoined to the pronoun هم; (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (من طين) attached to (خلقناهم)..
The clause «استفتهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أهم أشدّ ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «خلقنا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «إنّا خلقناهم..» has no grammatical position: giving the reason.
The clause «خلقناهم..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(استفتهم): it contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) in keeping with its indeclinable (mabnī) form; its imperfect is يستفتي, and its pattern is استفعهم.
(لازب): an active participle of the three-letter verb لزب, meaning "sticking to the hand"; its pattern is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:12-17.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) before يسخرون..
The clause «عجبت..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يسخرون..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هم.. and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(13- 14) (الواو) conjunction in the six places, and (الواو) in (ذكّروا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (لا) negating..
The clause «ذكّروا ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «لا يذكرون..» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a condition that does not put the verb in the jussive.
The clause «رأوا ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يستسخرون» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(15) (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (سحر) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هذا.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «إن هذا إلّا سحر ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(16) (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation in both places; (ترابا) the khabar of كنّا, accusative; (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb and its ism; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
The clause «متنا ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كنّا ترابا» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause متنا.
The clause «إنّا لمبعوثون» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the implied apodosis [Note: This clause cannot validly be the apodosis of the condition, so that the adverb is not attached to the khabar of إنّ, since what comes after (إنّ) does not govern what comes before it; so the attachment is implied, i.e. أإذا متنا ... نبعث "When we have died ... shall we be raised?", and the clause mentioned is an explanation of this implied element.].
(17) (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation, and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (آباؤنا) is omitted, its implied form being مبعوثون ...
The clause «آباؤنا ... (مبعوثون)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّا لمبعوثون.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(نعم) a particle of response; (الواو) conjunction — or circumstantial (ḥāliyya). The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنتم داخرون ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the implied clause that is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), i.e. نعم تبعثون وأنتم داخرون "Yes, you will be raised, and you will be humbled" [Note: Or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of the implied تبعثون.].

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) giving the reason; (إنّما) a restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa); (هي) a pronoun referring to the notion of the resurrection, or the Hour, or the cry of the Hereafter evident in the context, and it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being زجرة; (الفاء) conjunction; (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya) ...
The clause «إنّما هي زجرة ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption giving the reason for an implied prohibition, i.e. لا تستصعبوا ذلك فإنّما هي ... "Do not deem that difficult, for it is only ...".
The clause «هم ينظرون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause هي زجرة.
The clause «ينظرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(زجرة): a maṣdar of once-ness (maṣdar marra) of the three-letter verb زجر of the نصر class; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (يا) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ويلنا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb that is not in use ...
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause هي زجرة [Note: In the preceding verse (19).].
The clause «يا ويلنا..» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) — or parenthetical. The clause «هذا يوم الدين....» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied saying, i.e. the angels said: هذا يوم الدين "This is the Day of Judgement" [Note: Or the object of their own saying after the parenthesis يا ويلنا.].
(21) (الذي) a relative in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of يوم الفصل; (به) attached to (تكذّبون)..
The clause «هذا يوم الفصل ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption [Note: Whether it is from the speech of the disbelievers to one another or from the speech of the angels.].
The clause «كنتم به تكذّبون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «تكذّبون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(الفصل): a maṣdar (verbal noun) known by hearsay (samāʿī) of the three-letter verb فصل of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:22-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (أزواجهم) conjoined to the relative noun, accusative [Note: Or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), accusative.. and Ibn Hishām denies that the wāw of accompaniment occurs in the Revelation at all.]; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to the relative الذين, and the referring pronoun is omitted.
The clause «احشروا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied saying from the Creator, the Exalted, to the angels.
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «كانوا....» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يعبدون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا.
(23) (من دون) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied referring pronoun, i.e. يعبدونه من دون الله "they worship it besides Allah"; (الفاء) conjunction — or linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (إلى صراط) attached to (اهدوهم).
The clause «اهدوهم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause احشروا [Note: Or it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. إن تمّ حسابهم فاهدوهم "If their reckoning is complete, then lead them"..
And the clause of the condition and the apodosis is parenthetical between the two conjoined elements.].
The clause «قفوهم..» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause اهدوهم [Note: Or conjoined to the clause احشروا..].
The clause «إنّهم مسئولون» has no grammatical position: a resumption giving the reason.

* Morphology:
(قفوهم): it contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf); it is a weak verb of the mithāl type (first radical weak), whose fāʾ is dropped in the imperative because its ʿayn has kasra in the imperfect; its pattern is علوهم..

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (لكم) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (لا) negating; (تناصرون) an imperfect verb from which one of the two تاء's has been dropped.
The clause «ما لكم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied saying, i.e. that is said to them by way of rebuke.
The clause «لا تناصرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (اليوم) attached to the khabar (predicate) (مستسلمون).
The clause «هم اليوم مستسلمون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مستسلمون): plural of مستسلم, an active participle of the six-letter verb استسلم; its pattern is مستفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (على بعض) attached to (أقبل) ...
The clause «أقبل بعضهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يتساءلون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of أقبل.

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(عن اليمين) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent in (تأتوننا): swearing oaths..
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّكم كنتم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كنتم تأتوننا..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «تأتوننا ...» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(اليمين): a noun for an oath or for the well-known limb (the right hand); its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:29-32.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for nullifying digression (al-iḍrāb al-ibṭālī) ...
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لم تكونوا مؤمنين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) is implied, i.e. ما أضللناكم بل لم تكونوا مؤمنين ... "We did not lead you astray; rather you were not believers ...".
(30) (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negating; (لنا) attached to the khabar (predicate) of كان; (عليكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of سلطان; (بل) like the first ...
The clause «ما كان لنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لم تكونوا [Note: Or in the position of accusative, conjoined to the implied clause that is the object of the saying.].
The clause «كنتم قوما ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the saying.
(31- 32) (الفاء) conjunction carrying the meaning of cause; (علينا) attached to (حقّ); (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (اللام) for emphasis.
The clause «حقّ علينا قول ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّا لذائقون» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying [Note: In the verse there is a shift (iltifāt) from address to the first person, the original being: إنكم لذائقون "you will surely taste".. Or it is from the speech of those who led astray, giving the reason for what preceded, so it has no grammatical position.].
The clause «أغويناكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason.
The clause «كنّا غاوين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(طاغين): plural of طاغ, an active participle of the three-letter verb طغى; its pattern is فاع. It contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf), because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ) whose lām — the yāʾ — was omitted because it met, being quiescent, with the sukūn of the tanwīn; and likewise طاغين, on the pattern فاعين.

* Benefits:
- Giving the hamza of إن fatḥa or kasra:
1- Giving the hamza of إن fatḥa or kasra:
1- The hamza of (إن) takes fatḥa if it can validly be interpreted, together with its ism and khabar, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as in His saying, the Exalted, قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ, the implied sense being: "the listening of a group of jinn"; and our saying يعجبني أنك مخلص "It pleases me that you are sincere", the implied sense being: "your sincerity".
2- But if it cannot validly be interpreted, together with its ism and khabar, as a maṣdar, then it takes kasra, and the places where it takes kasra are in the following cases:
1- At the beginning of speech: as in His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّا أَعْطَيْناكَ الْكَوْثَرَ; or at the beginning of a resumed clause, as in His saying, the Exalted, فَلا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ ما يُسِرُّونَ وَما يُعْلِنُونَ. 2- After the verb of saying: as in the verse we are dealing with, which is His saying, the Exalted, قالُوا: إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ, and His saying, the Exalted, قالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ.
3- After an oath: as in His saying, the Exalted, وَالْعَصْرِ إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ, يس وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ. 4- If it occurs at the head of the ṣila (relative clause), as in His saying, the Exalted, ما إِنَّ مَفاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوأُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ أُولِي الْقُوَّةِ, and our saying (هذا الذي إنه محسن للمساكين) "This is the one who is kind to the poor".
5- If the لام is joined to its khabar, it takes kasra after it had the right to fatḥa, e.g.:
(علمت أنك صادق) "I knew that you were truthful" becomes (علمت إنك لصادق).

safi-cedvel:33-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative, attached to the khabar (predicate) (مشتركون); (في العذاب) attached to (مشتركون).
The clause «إنّهم ... مشتركون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(34) - (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is نفعل; (بالمجرمين) attached to (نفعل).
The clause «إنّا ... نفعل» has no grammatical position: parenthetical — or giving the reason. (35) - (لهم) attached to (قيل); (إلّا) a particle of exception; (الله) the Name of Majesty, a badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun in the implied khabar.
The clause «إنّهم كانوا.. يستكبرون» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for what preceded.
The clause «كانوا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «قيل لهم ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «لا إله إلّا الله ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied saying, i.e. قولوا لا إله.. "Say: there is no god..", and the implied clause of saying is in the position of nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: Because it is the object of the saying in the active verb..].
The clause «يستكبرون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا [Note: This is if the adverb (إذا) is devoid of conditional meaning, and what lies between the verb and its khabar is parenthetical ...
If the adverb is made to include the meaning of a condition, then the clause يستكبرون is its apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the condition, its protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of كانوا.].
(36) - (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation; (إنّا) like the first; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (لشاعر) attached to (تاركو).
The clause «يقولون ...» is conjoined to the clause يستكبرون.
The clause «أإنا لتاركو» .. is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(مشتركون): plural of مشترك, an active participle of the five-letter verb اشترك; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for nullifying digression (al-iḍrāb al-ibṭālī); (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of جاء ...
The clause «جاء ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: It is in reality a resumption within the scope of an implied saying, i.e. He, the Exalted, said: «ليس بشاعر بل جاء بالحقّ» "He is not a poet; rather he has brought the truth".].
The clause «صدّق ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:38-40.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
The clause «إنّكم لذائقو ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: And it is within the scope of the implied saying preceding in verse (37).].
(39) - (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negating, and (الواو) in (تجزون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the referring pronoun being omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ...) is in the position of accusative as the direct object, its governor being تجزون [Note: Or in the position of [Translator's note: the source has «في محل حرف جرّ» "in the position of a preposition"; «في محل جرّ» "in the position of genitive" is evidently intended.] genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the باء, attached to (تجزون).].
The clause «ما تجزون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كنتم تعملون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كنتم.
(40) (إلّا) a particle of exception; (عباد) accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) from the agent pronoun in (تعملون) ...

* Rhetoric:
Shift of person (iltifāt): in His saying, the Exalted, «إِنَّكُمْ لَذائِقُوا الْعَذابِ الْأَلِيمِ».
He shifted from the third person to direct address, to show the fullness of anger against them, by confronting them face to face with this threat, and by paying no heed to them. And that is what befits the arrogant.

safi-cedvel:41-49.t:
* I'rab:
(لهم) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) رزق..
The clause «أولئك لهم رزق ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لهم رزق ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
(42- 44) - (فواكه) a badal (substitute) of رزق, nominative [Note: Or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, and the clause is an adjective.]; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (في جنّات) attached to (مكرمون) [Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (مكرمون); it may also be a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.]; (على سرر) attached to (مكرمون) [Note: Or attached to متقابلين.]; (متقابلين) a ḥāl, accusative, of the pronoun in (مكرمون) ...
The clause «هم مكرمون..» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in (لهم) [Note: It may be in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لهم رزق.].
(45) (عليهم) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb يطاف; (بكأس) attached to (يطاف); (من معين) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of كأس.
The clause «يطاف عليهم ...» is in the position of nominative as another khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك) [Note: It may be resumptive, so it has no grammatical position.].
(46- 47) (بيضاء) a second naʿt of كأس, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, a diptote; (لذّة) a third naʿt, genitive; (للشاربين) attached to لذّة; (لا) negating; (فيها) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ غول; (الواو) conjunction; the second (لا) is redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation, and the redundancy is obligatory; (عنها) attached to (ينزفون), and (عن) is causal ...
The clause «لا فيها غول ...» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of كأس..
The clause «هم عنها ينزفون ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause لا فيها غول.
The clause «ينزفون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(48- 49) (الواو) conjunction; (عندهم) an adverb, accusative, attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ قاصرات; (عين) a naʿt of قاصرات, nominative.
The clause «عند هم قاصرات ...» is conjoined to the clause يطاف عليهم.
The clause «كأنهنّ بيض ...» is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of قاصرات.

* Morphology:
(45) كأس: a noun for the vessel one drinks from, and it is feminine; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; the plural is كؤوس — with ḍamma on the kāf — and أكؤس — with fatḥa on the first hamza — and كاسات, and كئاس with kasra on the kāf.
(46) (لذّة): feminine of لذّ, on the pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the past verb لذّ of the فتح class.. or it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the aforementioned verb; and if it is the maṣdar it mostly keeps the masculine. لذّة is a noun meaning the opposite of pain, and the plural is لذّات.
(47) غول: a maṣdar known by hearsay (samāʿī) of the three-letter verb غاله يغوله meaning "destroyed him", or غالته الخمر, i.e. the wine took away his mind or the health of his body; and it may be a noun meaning headache, drunkenness or hardship ... Its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(ينزفون): a verb always used in the passive form while having an active meaning, meaning "his mind went" or "he became drunk", in the same way as يهرع, يغمى عليه, يجنّ ... etc.; its past is نزف with ḍamma then kasra.
(48) قاصرات: plural of قاصرة, the feminine of قاصر, an active participle of the three-letter verb قصر of the نصر class: قصر عن الشيء when one refrains from it, i.e. restraining their glances from other than their husbands ... or قصر على الشيء, i.e. one did not aspire to anything else and did not go beyond it to another.
(عين): plural of عيناء, a resembling adjective from عين يعين of the فرح class, i.e. the black of whose eye is large and wide; its pattern is فعلاء; and the pattern of عين is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn, its fāʾ having been given kasra to suit the yāʾ, for lightness; the masculine is أعين on the pattern أفعل.
(49) بيض: a generic noun (ism jins) for what females of animals and others produce (eggs); the singular is بيضة, on the pattern فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn, and the pattern of بيض is فعل with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(مكنون): a passive participle of the three-letter verb (كنّ); its pattern is مفعول.
The loose simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in His saying, the Exalted, «كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَكْنُونٌ».
What is meant is likening them to eggs sheltered by feathers in the nest, which hands have not touched and dust has not reached, with a slight yellowness together with a lustre as in pearls. Most hold that it is specifically ostrich eggs in their nests in the sand, because they are finer in appearance than all other eggs, and further from the touch of hands and from anything reaching them that would change their colour. The Arabs liken women to eggs, and they call them "eggs of the curtained chambers"; from this is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وبيضة خدر لا يرام خباؤها ... تمتعت من لهو بها غير معجل
(Many an egg of the curtained chamber, whose tent none dared approach, have I enjoyed sporting with, unhurried.)

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (أقبل ... يتساءلون) the i'rab of this verse has passed [Note: See verse (27) of this sūra, words and clauses.].

safi-cedvel:51-53.t:
* I'rab:
(منهم) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of قائل; (لي) attached to the khabar (predicate) of كان..
The clause «قال قائل ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «إنّي كان لي قرين» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كان لي قرين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(52) The fāʿil (agent) of (يقول) is a pronoun referring to القرين; (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (من المصدّقين) attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يقول ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of قرين.
The clause «أإنّك لمن المصدّقين» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
(53) (أإذا متنا.. لمدينون) the i'rab of its counterpart has passed [Note: See verse (16) of this sūra, words and clauses.]..

safi-cedvel:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
The fāʿil (agent) of (قال) is a pronoun referring to the aforementioned speaker; (هل) a particle of interrogation.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنتم مطّلعون» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(مطّلعون): plural of مطّلع, an active participle of the five-letter verb اطّلع; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.. The word contains a substitution (ibdāl): its original form is مطتلع, taken from اطتلع.. the تاء came after the طاء, was changed into a طاء and assimilated into the first طاء..

safi-cedvel:55-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction in both places; (في سواء) attached to (رآه).
The clause «اطّلع ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال [Note: In the preceding verse (54).].
The clause «رآه....» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اطّلع.

safi-cedvel:56-59.t:
* I'rab:
(التاء) the tāʾ of the oath, putting the noun in the genitive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, genitive by (التاء), attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم "I swear"; (إن) lightened from the heavy (inna), necessarily inoperative (muhmala); (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), redundant (zāʾida); and (النون) in (تردين) is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and (الياء), omitted for lightness, is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the oath and its answer ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كدت لتردين» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.
The clause «تردين..» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كدت.
(57) (الواو) conjunction; (لولا) a conditional particle that does not put the verb in the jussive; (نعمة) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and the khabar is obligatorily omitted; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لولا; (من المحضرين) attached to the khabar of كنت..
The clause «لولا نعمة ربّي ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer to the oath.
The clause «كنت من المحضرين» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(58) (الهمزة) for interrogation; (الفاء) conjunction; (ما) negating, operating like ليس; (ميّتين) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ما.
The clause «ما نحن بميّتين ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object of an implied saying, i.e. the people of Paradise said: «أنحن مخلّدون فما نحن بميّتين ...» "Are we immortal, so that we shall not die ...?"
(59) (إلّا) a particle of exception; (موتتنا) accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) [Note: It is said that (إلّا) is for restriction (ḥaṣr) and (موتتنا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is the resembling adjective (ميّتين).]; (الواو) conjunction; (ما نحن بمعذّبين) like ما نحن بميّتين.
The clause «ما نحن بمعذّبين ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause ما نحن بميّتين.

* Morphology:
(كدت): it contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf), because it is a hollow verb (ajwaf) to which a nominative pronoun is attached: when it was made indeclinable on the sukūn and two quiescent letters met, the alif and the dāl, the alif was omitted. Its pattern is فلت with kasra on the fāʾ; its class is فرح, the vowel of the omitted ʿayn having been transferred to the fāʾ; its original form is كود يكود, like خوف يخوف.
(موتتنا): a maṣdar of once-ness (maṣdar marra) from مات, on the pattern فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:60-61.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (لمثل) attached to (يعمل); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (اللام) the lām of command, and the verb (يعمل) was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters..
The clause «إنّ هذا لهو الفوز ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو الفوز ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «ليعمل العاملون ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. من أراد الفوز في الآخرة فليعمل له مثل ذلك في الدنيا "Whoever wants success in the Hereafter, let him work for it likewise in this world".

safi-cedvel:62-68.t:
* I'rab:
(نزلا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (أم) a conjunction counterbalancing the hamza of interrogation; (شجرة) conjoined to the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ذلك).
The clause «ذلك خير ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(63) - (للظالمين) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of فتنة — or to فتنة. The clause «إنّا جعلناها ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «جعلناها ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
(64- 65) - (في أصل) attached to (تخرج), by making it include the meaning of تنبت "it grows".
The clause «إنّها شجرة ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption.
The clause «تخرج ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of شجرة.
The clause «طلعها كأنّه رؤوس ...» is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of شجرة.
The clause «كأنّه رؤوس ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ طلعها.
(66) (الفاء) resumptive; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (منها) attached to (آكلون), and the second is attached to (مالئون), which is conjoined to (آكلون) by (الفاء); (البطون) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle مالئون.
The clause «إنّهم لآكلون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(67) (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar; (عليها) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of حميم [Note: An adjective placed before what it qualifies, i.e. إنّ لهم لشوبا من حميم مصبوب على ما يأكلون من شجرة الزقّوم "they will have a mixture of scalding water poured over what they eat of the tree of Zaqqūm".]; (اللام) for emphasis; (شوبا) the ism of إنّ, accusative; (من حميم) attached to a naʿt of (شوبا)..
The clause «إن لهم.. لشوبا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّهم لآكلون.
(68) - (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis; (إلى الجحيم) attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّ مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّ لهم.. لشوبا.

* Morphology:
(62) الزقّوم: a noun for the fruit of a vile, bitter tree of loathsome taste; it is said to be a tree found in the land of Tihāma, among the vilest of trees; its pattern is فعّول with fatḥa, and ḍamma on the doubled ʿayn.
(64) أصل: a noun for the lowest part of a thing, or what is opposite to the branch, or it is the maṣdar (verbal noun); its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.. from the three-letter verb of the كرم class.
(66) مالئون: plural of مالئ, an active participle of the three-letter verb ملأ; its pattern is فاعل.
(67) شوبا: a maṣdar known by hearsay (samāʿī) of the verb شابه يشوبه, i.e. mixed with it; it may be intended as the passive participle, i.e. المشوب "mixed"; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metaphor (istiʿāra): in His saying, the Exalted, «طَلْعُها».
Al-ṭalʿ belongs to the date-palm, and it was borrowed for what emerges from the tree of Zaqqūm of its yield: either a verbal metaphor or a conceptual one.
2- The imaginative simile (al-tashbīh al-takhyīlī): in His saying, the Exalted, «طَلْعُها كَأَنَّهُ رُؤُسُ الشَّياطِينِ».
It is likened to the heads of devils as an indication of its utmost loathsomeness and ugliness of appearance, because the devil is loathed and considered ugly in people's natures, as they believe him to be pure evil unmixed with any good; so they say of one with an ugly form: "as if it were the face of a devil, as if it were the head of a devil". And when painters depict him, they bring his image in the ugliest and most terrifying form imaginable; just as they believed the angel to be pure good with no evil in it, so they likened a beautiful form to it. Allah the Exalted said: «ما هذا بَشَراً إِنْ هذا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ».
3- The secret of conjoining with «ثم»: in His saying, the Exalted, «ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْها لَشَوْباً مِنْ حَمِيمٍ» there is a secret, subtle in derivation and fine in its path, for in the meaning of delay (tarākhī) there are two aspects. The first: that they fill their bellies from the tree of Zaqqūm, which is hot, burning their bellies and making them thirsty, and they are not given drink until after a long while, as a torment by that thirst; then they are given to drink what is hotter, namely the drink mixed with scalding water. The second: that He mentioned the food with that loathsomeness and repulsiveness, then mentioned the drink with what is more loathsome and repulsive, so He brought ثم to indicate the remoteness of the state of the drink from the state of the food, and the difference of its description from that of the food in exceeding it.

safi-cedvel:69-70.t:
* I'rab:
(ألفوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (ضالّين) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «إنّهم ألفوا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption giving the reason.
The clause «ألفوا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
(70) - (الفاء) conjunction; (على آثارهم) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هم..
And (الواو) in (يهرعون) is the fāʿil [Note: It should be noted that this verb is used in the language only in the passive form, so the pronoun in it must be an agent, not a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil).].
The clause «هم على آثارهم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّهم ألفوا.
The clause «يهرعون..» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of "being settled" (istiqrār).].

* Morphology:
(ألفوا): it contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, the lām of the word and the (واو) of the plural; the letter before the wāw was given fatḥa as an indication of the omitted alif; its pattern is أفعوا — with fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:71-74.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قبلهم) an adverb, accusative, attached [Translator's note: the source reads «متعلّق لا متعلّق ب (ضلّ)», which appears garbled; the sense is "attached to (ضلّ)".] to (ضلّ) [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of أكثر.] ...
The clause «ضلّ ... أكثر» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath ...
The implied oath clause has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(72) (فيهم) attached to (أرسلنا), by making it include the meaning of بعثنا "We sent forth"..
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first implied oath clause.
(73) - (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كان..
The clause «انظر ...» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: إن عاقبنا المنذرين. فانظر ... "If We punished those who were warned, then look ...".
The clause «كان عاقبة ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. (74) - (إلّا) for exception; (عباد) accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) ...

safi-cedvel:75-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (الفاء) conjunction; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for the preceding implied oath; (نعم) a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; (المجيبون) fāʿil (agent), nominative ... and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, its implied form being نحن "We".
The clause «نادانا نوح ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.
The clause «نعم المجيبون..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer to the oath [Note: Or the answer to another implied oath.].
(76) - (الواو) conjunction in the following four places; (أهله) conjoined to the third-person pronoun in (نجّيناه); (من الكرب) attached to (نجّيناه)..
The clause «نجّيناه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause that is the answer to the oath.
(77) - (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); (الباقين) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being جعلنا.
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجّيناه.
(78) - (عليه) attached to an omitted element which is the object of تركنا, i.e. تركنا ثناء عليه "We left praise of him"..
(في الآخرين) attached to (تركنا).
The clause «تركنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجّيناه.
(79) - (سلام) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative [Note: Beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible because it indicates a supplication.]; (على نوح) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ سلام; (في العالمين) attached to the "being settled" (istiqrār), which is the khabar.
The clause «سلام على نوح» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication [Note: Or it is an explanation of His saying تركنا ... or an explanation of the implied object, i.e. "We left something, which is these words" ... It may also be the object of an implied saying, i.e. قلنا سلام ... "We said: Peace ...".].
(80) - (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is نجزي ...
The clause «إنّا ... نجزي ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for what preceded.
The clause «نجزي ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(81) - (من عبادنا) attached to an omitted khabar of إنّ..
The clause «إنّه من عبادنا ...» has no grammatical position: another reason.
(82) - (ثمّ) a conjunction ...
The clause «أغرقنا....» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجّيناه — or جعلنا.

* Morphology:
(75) المجيبون: plural of المجيب, an active participle of the four-letter verb أجاب; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. It contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb): its original form is مجوب — with kasra on the wāw, for it has wāw as its ʿayn — then the wāw was given sukūn and its vowel was transferred to the jīm, then the wāw was changed into a yāʾ because the letter before it has kasra, so it became (مجيب) [Note: And see verse (61) of Sūrat Hūd.].

safi-cedvel:83-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من شيعته) attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (اللام) for emphasis; (إبراهيم) the ism of إنّ, accusative.
The clause «إنّ من شيعته لإبراهيم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(84) (إذ) an adverb of past time, attached to an omitted element indicated by the word شيعته, i.e. شايعه إذ جاء ربّه "he followed him when he came to his Lord"; (بقلب) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent.
The clause «جاء ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
(85) - (إذ) an adverb, a badal (substitute) of the first; (لأبيه) attached to (قال); (ماذا) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being تعبدون [Note: Or (ما) is an interrogative, mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar being the relative noun (ذا), and the clause of the mubtadaʾ and khabar is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause تعبدون is a ṣila (relative clause), the referring pronoun being omitted.].
The clause «قال ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تعبدون..» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
(86) (الهمزة) for rebuking interrogation; (إفكا) a fronted direct object, accusative [Note: It is said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) whose governor is تريدون, and the direct object is آلهة.]; (آلهة) a badal of (إفكا) with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. عبادة آلهة "the worship of gods"; (دون) an adverb, accusative, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of آلهة [Note: Or attached to (تريدون).].
The clause «تريدون» is in the position of accusative as a badal of the clause تعبدون.

safi-cedvel:123-132.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (من المرسلين) attached to the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «إنّ إلياس لمن المرسلين» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
(124) (إذ) an adverb of past time, attached to (المرسلين) [Note: or a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (اذكر).]; (لقومه) attached to (قال); (ألا) a particle of urging (ʿarḍ) with no grammatical effect.
The clause «قال ... » is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
The clause «ألا تتّقون ... » is in the position of an accusative, being the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
(125) (الهمزة) for rebuking question (istifhām inkārī); (الواو) a conjunction.
The clause «تدعون ... » is in the position of an accusative, a badal (substitute) for the clause تتّقون.
The clause «تذرون..» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause تدعون.
(126-128) (الله) the Majestic Name, a badal (substitute) for أحسن, accusative - or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it; (ربّكم) a naʿt (adjective) of the Majestic Name - or a badal of it - accusative; (الفاء) a conjunction, and the second one is a connecting particle for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis; (إلّا) for exception; (عباد) excepted by إلّا, accusative.
The clause «كذّبوه ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause قال ...
The clause «إنّهم لمحضرون..» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if their reckoning comes, then they ..."
(129-132) (وتركنا ... من عبادنا المؤمنين) the i'rab of its parallels has already been given [Note: in verses (78, 79, 80, 81) of this sūra.], both words and clauses.

* Morphology:
(123) إلياس: a proper name of one of the prophets of the Children of Israel; it is said that he is Idrīs, and Ibn ʿAbbās said that he is the cousin of al-Yasaʿ, and it is said that he is the nephew of Hārūn. It is a non-Arabic (aʿjamī) proper name whose wazn (pattern) is not known.
(125) بعلا: a noun meaning "god"; its wazn is فعل (with fatḥa and sukūn).
(130) إلياسين: it is said that it is another name of Ilyās, so it is singular; and it is said that it is a sound masculine plural (jamʿ mudhakkar sālim) for everyone who believed with Ilyās, by way of predominance (taghlīb), as one says "the Muhallabs" and "the Ashʿarīs" in reference to al-Muhallab and al-Ashʿarī. In origin it is the plural of إلياسيّ - a nisba (relative adjective) to Ilyās - then the shadda on the yāʾ was found heavy and one of the two yāʾs was dropped; then, when it was pluralised as a sound masculine plural, two sukūns met, one of the two yāʾs and the plural yāʾ, and the first of them was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, so it became إلياسين. The view that it is singular is sounder.

* Benefits:
- The story of Ilyās, peace be upon him:
Qatāda and Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: Ilyās is Idrīs. Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: my father narrated to us, Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us from Abū Isḥāq from ʿUbayda ibn Rabīʿa from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd - may Allah be pleased with him - who said: Ilyās is Idrīs. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said the same.
Wahb ibn Munabbih said: he is Ilyās ibn (Yāsīn) ibn Finḥās ibn al-ʿAyzār ibn Hārūn ibn ʿImrān. Allah sent him to the Children of Israel after Ḥizqīl, peace be upon them both. They had worshipped an idol called "Baʿl", so he called them to Allah and forbade them from worshipping anything besides Him. Their king had believed in him, then apostatised, and they continued in their error, and none of them believed in him. So he prayed to Allah against them, and Allah withheld the rain from them for three years. Then they asked him to remove that from them and promised to believe in him if the rain reached them. He prayed to Allah for them, and the rain came to them, but they continued in the vilest of their former disbelief. So he asked Allah to take him to Himself. Al-Yasaʿ ibn Akhṭūb - peace be upon him - had grown up under his care, and Ilyās was commanded to go to such-and-such a place, and that whatever came to him there he should mount it and not fear it. A horse of fire came to him and he mounted it; Allah clothed him in light and dressed him in feathers, and he would fly with the angels, an angel in human form, heavenly and earthly. Thus Wahb related it from the People of the Book. And Allah knows best whether it is sound.

safi-cedvel:133-138.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لمن المرسلين) the shifted lām and the khabar of inna.
The clause «إنّ لوطا لمن المرسلين» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
(135-136) (إذ) an adverb of past time, attached to (المرسلين) [Note: or it is an adverbial noun in the position of an accusative, a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (اذكر).]; in the position of an accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (أهله) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the third-person pronoun in (نجيناه), accusative; (أجمعين) a semantic tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun of Lūṭ and his family; (إلّا) for exception; (عجوزا) excepted by إلّا, accusative; (في الغابرين) a naʿt (adjective) of (عجوزا).
The clause «نجّيناه ... » is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
The clause «دمّرنا ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause نجّيناه.
(137) (الواو) a conjunction; (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis; (عليهم) attached to (تمرّون); (مصبحين) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the fāʿil (agent) of تمرّون.
The clause «إنّكم لتمرّون ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّ لوطا لمن المرسلين.
The clause «تمرّون..» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
(138) (الواو) a conjunction; (بالليل) attached to a ḥāl conjoined to the preceding ḥāl; (الهمزة) for a reproachful question (istifhām tawbīkhī); (الفاء) a conjunction; (لا) negative.
The clause «لا تعقلون ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied clause, that is:
"Are you heedless of that, so you do not reason?"

* Benefits:
- The pronoun:
The pronoun is divided into three types:
1- The detached pronoun (al-ḍamīr al-munfaṣil): it is the one that comes independently, not attached to anything, and it is of two kinds:
a- Pronouns of the nominative: أنا - نحن - أنت - أنت - أنتما - أنتم - أنتن - هو - هي - هما - هم - هن.
b- Pronouns of the accusative: إيّاي - إيّانا - إيّاك.. etc.
2- The latent pronoun (al-ḍamīr al-mustatir): it is the one that does not appear in speech but is only implied, and it is:
for the third person: هو - هي. For the first person: أنا - نحن. For the second person: أنت.
As for the remaining pronouns such as أنتما - هما - هم, they do not come latent; only the pronouns we have mentioned are latent. The pronoun is latent permissibly (jawāzan) with the third person: هو - هي. And it is latent obligatorily (wujūban) with the first and second person: أنا - نحن - أنت.
3- The attached pronoun (al-ḍamīr al-muttaṣil): it is the pronoun that is attached to a word and does not come independently. It may be attached to a noun such as (كتابك), or to a verb such as (جاؤوا), or to a particle such as (عليه). It is divided into three kinds:
a- Pronouns specific to the nominative, namely: the alif of the dual - the wāw of the group - the yāʾ of the (feminine) addressee - the vowelled tāʾ - the nūn of the feminine plural.
These pronouns attach only to a verb. If the verb is complete (not defective), they are in the position of a nominative, a fāʿil (agent), as in the verse we are dealing with, His saying, the Exalted, أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ
for the wāw of the group is an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative, fāʿil. But if it is attached to a defective verb (kāna and its sisters), it is in the position of a nominative, its ism (subject).
b- Pronouns specific to the accusative and genitive, namely: the hāʾ of the third person, the yāʾ of the first person, and the kāf of the addressee. They share in attaching to a verb, a noun, a particle, or the particles resembling the verb (inna and its sisters). If attached to a verb, they are in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), such as (أكرمتك); if attached to a particle resembling the verb, they are in the position of an accusative, its ism; if attached to a noun, they are in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); and if attached to a particle (that is, a preposition), they are in the position of a genitive by the preposition.
c- And a pronoun that serves the nominative, the accusative or the genitive, and it is (نا): it comes sometimes in the position of a nominative such as (سمعنا وأطعنا), sometimes in the position of a genitive such as (ربنا), and sometimes in the position of an accusative such as (لا تؤاخذنا).
Note: if the yāʾ of the first person attaches to one of the two prepositions (من) and (عن), or to a verb, the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) is brought in as a separator between the yāʾ and what precedes it, such as: منّي - عنّي - أكرمني - يكرمني - أكرمني..

safi-cedvel:139-148.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لمن المرسلين) like the preceding [Note: in verse (133)].
The clause «إنّ يونس لمن المرسلين» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
(140) (إذ أبق) like إذ نجّيناه [Note: in verse (134) of this sūra.]; (إلى الفلك) attached to (أبق).
The clause «أبق ... » is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
(141) (الفاء) a conjunction in both places; (من المدحضين) attached to the khabar of kāna.
The clause «ساهم ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause أبق.
The clause «كان من المدحضين..» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause ساهم.
(142) (الفاء) a conjunction and (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
The clause «التقمه الحوت ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause كان ...
The clause «هو مليم» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
(143) (الفاء) resumptive - or a conjunction; (لولا) a non-jussive conditional particle; (من المسبّحين) attached to the khabar of kāna.
The interpreted maṣdar (المصدر المؤوّل) (أنّه كان من المسبّحين) is in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "present" (موجود).
The clause «لولا (تسبيحه) موجود» has no grammatical position, resumptive - or conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «كان من المسبّحين» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of anna.
(144) (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لولا; (في بطنه) attached to (لبث) [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl from the fāʿil of لبث.]; (إلى يوم) attached to (لبث); and the (الواو) in (يبعثون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «لبث ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يبعثون» is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
(145) (الفاء) resumptive; (بالعراء) attached to (نبذناه), and (الباء) denotes location (ẓarfiyya); (الواو) circumstantial.
The clause «نبذناه ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive, in the course of the story of Yūnus.
The clause «هو سقيم» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
(146) (الواو) a conjunction; (عليه) attached to (أنبتنا), by including in it the meaning of ظلّلنا ("we shaded"); (من يقطين) attached to a naʿt of (شجرة).
The clause «أنبتنا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نبذناه.
(147) (الواو) a conjunction; (إلى مائة) attached to (أرسلناه); (أو) for iḍrāb (turning from one statement to another) [Note: The commentators differed greatly on the meaning of (أو): it is said to be for iḍrāb, it is said to be for vagueness (ibhām), it is said to be for mere joining, it is said to be for choice (takhyīr), and it is said to be for permission (ibāḥa).]..
The clause «أرسلناه ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نبذناه..
The clause «يزيدون..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(148) (الفاء) a conjunction in both places; (إلى حين) attached to (متّعناهم).
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أرسلناه.
The clause «متّعناهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمنوا.

* Morphology:
(141) المدحضين: plural of المدحض, a passive participle from the passive أدحض; its wazn is مفعل (with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn).
(142) مليم: an active participle from the quadriliteral ألام, as in "so-and-so ألام" when he does what deserves blame; its wazn is مفعل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn). It contains an i'lāl (weakening) by substitution and an i'lāl by quiescence: its origin is ملوم (ḍamma, sukūn, kasra); the kasra was found heavy on the wāw, so it was made quiescent - i'lāl by quiescence - and its vowel was moved to the lām before it; then the wāw was turned into a yāʾ because of the kasra before the wāw, so it became مليم.
(143) المسبّحين: plural of المسبّح, an active participle from the quadriliteral سبّح; its wazn is مفعّل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn).
(145) العراء: a name for the surface of the earth, an inert noun (jāmid); its hamza is converted from a yāʾ, its origin being العراي, because it is from عري يعرى (of the pattern فرح); when the yāʾ came at the end after a quiescent alif, it was turned into a hamza.
(146) يقطين: an inert noun for the gourd plant, its wazn is يفعيل (with fatḥa on the yāʾ), derived from قطن بالمكان when one stays in it and does not leave.

* Benefits:
- Yūnus ﷺ and the ship:
Ibn ʿAbbās and Wahb said: Yūnus - peace be upon him - had promised his people punishment, but the punishment was delayed for them, so he went out as one hiding from them, made for the sea, and boarded the ship. The ship was held back, and the sailors said: "Here is a slave who has run away from his master." They cast lots, and it fell on Yūnus three times. He said: "I am the runaway," and threw himself into the water. This is what Ibn ʿAbbās said. Then the whale swallowed him, and he was glorifying Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and remembering Him often. Ibn ʿAbbās said: he was one of those who pray. Some of them said: "Remember Allah in times of ease and He will remember you in times of hardship." The reports differ on the length of his stay in the belly of the whale: it is said three days, it is said seven, it is said twenty, and it is said forty. After the whale cast him out, Allah caused a plant of gourd (يقطين) to grow over him (meaning the gourd), a plant distinguished by flies not approaching it. Then Allah sent him to a hundred thousand or more, that is, rather more. It is reported in the hadith that they were more by (twenty thousand), and they believed in him.
It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb - may Allah be pleased with him - who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about His saying, the Exalted, وَأَرْسَلْناهُ إِلى مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ and he said: "They were more by twenty thousand." Al-Tirmidhī transmitted it,
and said: a good (ḥasan) hadith.
- (أو):
The statements of the grammarians conflicted about the meaning of (أو) in His saying, the Exalted: وَأَرْسَلْناهُ إِلى مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ. Ibn Hishām mentioned this disagreement in al-Mughnī and cited these views. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is (بل يزيدون), so it came in the exegesis, and it is sound in Arabic. Some of the Kufans said: it has the meaning of the wāw. The Basrans have several views: it is said it is for vagueness (ibhām); it is said
for choice (takhyīr), that is, when the observer sees them he may choose between saying "they are a hundred thousand" or "they are more" - Ibn al-Shajarī related this from Sībawayh, and its attribution to him is open to question - and choice between two things, one of which has occurred, is not valid; and it is said it is for doubt, referred to the observer - Ibn Jinnī mentioned it. Imam al-Nasafī cited in his exegesis the statement: (أو يزيدون) is in the sight of the observer, that is, when the observer sees them he says: "they are a hundred thousand or more." Al-Zajjāj said: more than one said that its meaning is "rather they were more"; al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayda said so, and it is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, and this view is the most evident. These are the views, and Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:149-157.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive, and the third-person pronoun in (استفتهم) refers to the disbelievers of Makka; (الهمزة) for a rebuking question (istifhām inkārī); (لربّك) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ البنات; (الواو) for a rebuking question, (لربّك) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ البنات [Translator's note: the source text repeats this phrase here, apparently by a copying error; it is translated as written.]; (الواو) a conjunction; (لهم البنون) like لربك البنات.
The clause «استفتهم..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ألربّك البنات..» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لهم البنون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the explanatory resumption.
(150) (أم) a conjunction equivalent to the hamza (muʿādila) [Note: or it is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) أم, meaning بل and the hamza, and the clause after it is resumptive.]; (إناثا) a ḥāl, accusative, from الملائكة; (الواو) circumstantial.
The clause «خلقنا....» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the explanatory resumption.
The clause «هم شاهدون» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
(151) (ألا) a particle of alerting; (من إفكهم) attached to (يقولون), and من denotes cause (sababiyya); (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis ...
The clause «إنّهم ... ليقولون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(152) (الواو) circumstantial; (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis.
The clause «ولد الله ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the speech [Note: They did not say these words explicitly; rather it follows necessarily from their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah.].
The clause «إنّهم لكاذبون» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
(153) (الهمزة) for a rebuking question; (على البنين) attached to (اصطفى).
The clause «اصطفى ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(154) (ما) an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ; (لكم) attached to an omitted khabar of ما; (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl whose operator is (تحكمون).
The clause «ما لكم....» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تحكمون ... » has no grammatical position, a badal from the clause ما لكم.
(155) (الهمزة) for a reproachful question; (الفاء) a conjunction; (لا) negative.
The clause «تذكّرون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, that is:
"Are you heedless, so you do not remember?"
(156) (أم) is the disconnected أم meaning بل and the hamza; (لكم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (سلطان).
The clause «لكم سلطان ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(157) (الفاء) a connecting particle for the apodosis of an implied condition; (بكتابكم) attached to (ائتوا); (كنتم) a defective past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
The clause «ائتوا ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you are truthful, then bring ..." [Note: or: "if you have a proof, then bring ..."].
The clause «إن كنتم صادقين ... » has no grammatical position, an explanation of the implied condition ... [Note: and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then bring your book ..."].

* Morphology:
(أصطفى): the hamzat al-waṣl (connecting hamza) was dropped because the interrogative hamza entered the verb, and the ṭāʾ is substituted for the tāʾ of the form iftiʿāl.
(تذكّرون): one of the two tāʾs was dropped for lightness, and its origin is تتذكّرون.

* Benefits:
- The entry of the interrogative hamza onto the hamzat al-waṣl:
1- If the interrogative hamza enters a hamzat al-waṣl (with kasra), we drop the hamzat al-waṣl, as in His saying, the Exalted, in the verse we are dealing with أَصْطَفَى الْبَناتِ عَلَى الْبَنِينَ and your saying (أسمك خالد) (أستغفرت الله).
2- But if it enters a hamzat al-waṣl with fatḥa, the two hamzas are merged and become a long alif, such as آللَّهُ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ آلْآنَ وَقَدْ عَصَيْتَ قَبْلُ

safi-cedvel:158-160.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive - or a conjunction; (بينه) an accusative adverb attached to an omitted second direct object; (بين) an adverb conjoined to the first and attached to what the first is attached to; (الواو) a conjunction; (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of certainty; (اللام) the shifted lām.. And the pronoun in (إنهم، محضرون) refers to the polytheists.
The clause «جعلوا....» has no grammatical position, resumptive - or conjoined to a preceding resumption.
The clause «علمت الجنّة ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath.. and the implied oath clause is conjoined to the clause جعلوا ...
The clause «إنّهم لمحضرون..» is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of علمت, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by (إنّ); the hamza of inna has a kasra because the lām came with the khabar.
(159) (سبحان) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb; (ما) a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يصفون) is in the position of a genitive, attached to the omitted verb.
The clause « (نسبّح) سبحان..» has no grammatical position, parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) and supplicatory.
The clause «يصفون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-type relative (maṣdar).
(160) (إلّا) for exception; (عباد) excepted by إلّا from the fāʿil of جعلوا or from the pronoun in محضرون [Note: it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), and it may be a disconnected one if the one excepted from is the pronoun of (يصفون).].

* Morphology:
(الجنّة): they are the angels here, and they were so named because of their being hidden from sight; its wazn is فعلة (with kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn).

safi-cedvel:161-163.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive and (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the pronoun of the addressee in (إنّكم).
The clause «إنّكم ... ما أنتم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تعبدون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
(162) (ما) negative, working like ليس; (عليه) attached to (فاتنين); (فاتنين) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ما, and the object of فاتنين is omitted, that is, "anyone".
The clause «ما أنتم عليه بفاتنين» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
(163) (إلّا) for exception; (من) a relative noun in the position of an accusative by exception from the implied object [Note: the exception may be an emptied (mufarragh) one, with (من) as the direct object of the active participle فاتنين.]; (صال) a khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, dropped for lightness, in keeping with the reading in continuous speech ...
The clause «هو صال الجحيم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(فاتنين): plural of فاتن, an active participle from the triliteral فتن; its wazn is فاعل.
(صال): an active participle from صلي يصلى (of the pattern فرح); it came in the verse on the pattern فاع with the lām dropped, despite being in annexation.

safi-cedvel:164-166.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative, non-working; (منّا) attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the implied mubtadaʾ أحد; (إلّا) for restriction; (له) a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (مقام); and the pronoun in (منّا) refers to the angels [Note: and it is said that it refers to the Prophet and the believers.].
The clause «ما منا (أحد) ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «له مقام ... » is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the implied mubtadaʾ أحد. (165-166) - (الواو) a conjunction; (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb, with its ism; (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis.
The clause «إنّا لنحن ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما منّا ...
The clause «نحن الصافّون» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
The clause «إنّا لنحن (الثانية) » has no grammatical position, conjoined to إنّا لنحن..
(the first).
The clause «نحن المسبّحون» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna (the second).

* Benefits:
- The separating pronoun (ḍamīr al-faṣl):
In this verse occurs His saying, the Exalted, وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الصَّافُّونَ. The pronoun (نحن) is called the separating pronoun (ḍamīr al-faṣl), or the supporting one (ʿimād), because it strengthens the meaning of the sentence and emphasises it. Similar is His saying, the Exalted, كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ and إِنْ تَرَنِ أَنَا أَقَلَّ مِنْكَ مالًا وَوَلَداً.
The Basrans claimed that it has no grammatical position and is merely for emphasis, and most of them then said:
that it is a particle, so there is no difficulty. Al-Khalīl said: it is a noun, and its parallel on this view are the nouns of verbs (asmāʾ al-afʿāl), for those who consider them not governed by anything, and (أك) the relative [Translator's note: the source reads (أك) here; the intended word is unclear.]. The Kufans said: it has a position. Then al-Kisāʾī said: its position depends on what follows it, and al-Farrāʾ said: on what precedes it. So its position between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar is nominative; between the two objects of ẓanna, accusative; between the two operands of kāna, nominative according to al-Farrāʾ and accusative according to al-Kisāʾī; and between the two operands of inna, the reverse. A detailed discussion of this pronoun, which contains healing for what is in the breasts, will come.

safi-cedvel:167-170.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إن) lightened from the heavy (inna), whose non-operation is obligatory; (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa).. And the pronoun in (يقولون) refers to the disbelievers of Quraysh.
The clause «كانوا ليقولون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يقولون» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of كانوا.
(168) (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (عندنا) an accusative adverb attached to a fronted khabar; (من الأولين) a naʿt of (ذكرا) with an omitted muḍāf, that is, "from the books of the ancients".
The clause « (ثبت) ذكر ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the speech.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ عندنا ذكرا ... ) is in the position of a nominative, the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "was established" (ثبت), that is, the existence of the reminder was established.
(169) - (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو ...
The clause «كنّا عباد ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(170) (الفاء) a conjunction and the second a connecting particle for the apodosis of an implied condition; (سوف) a particle of futurity.
The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, that is:
"so it came to them, and they disbelieved ..."
The clause «سوف يعلمون» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if the time of their reckoning comes, then they will come to know the outcome of their disbelief."

safi-cedvel:171-179.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of certainty; (لعبادنا) attached to a ḥāl from كلمتنا, that is, "spoken for our servants".
The clause «سبقت كلمتنا ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the implied oath.
The implied oath clause has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(172-173) (اللام) is the shifted lām for emphasis in both places.
The clause «إنّهم لهم المنصورون» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption - or an explanation of the word (kalima). The clause: «هم المنصورون» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
The clause «إنّ جندنا لهم الغالبون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the explanatory one.
The clause «هم الغالبون» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna (the second).
(174) (الفاء) a connecting particle for the apodosis of an implied condition; (عنهم) attached to (تولّ); (حتّى حين) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تولّ).
The clause «تولّ عنهم ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if victory is for our soldiers, then turn away from them ..."
(175) (الواو) a conjunction; (الفاء) a connecting particle; (سوف) a particle of futurity.
The clause «أبصرهم ... » is conjoined to the clause تولّ.
The clause «سوف يبصرون» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you do, then they will see."
(176) (الهمزة) for a threatening question; (الفاء) resumptive; (بعذابنا) attached to (يستعجلون), by including in it the meaning of "they mock" [Note: or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "they mock", and the clause يستعجلون is a ḥāl from the fāʿil.].
The clause «يستعجلون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(177) (الفاء) a conjunction; (بساحتهم) attached to (نزل); (الفاء) a connecting particle for the apodosis; (ساء) a past verb for expressing censure (inshāʾ al-dhamm); (صباح) a fāʿil, nominative, and the specified object of censure (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "their morning".
The clause «نزل ... » is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
The clause «ساء صباح ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(178-179) (الواو) a conjunction; (تولّ ... يبصرون): their i'rab has just been given, in words [Note: in the preceding verses (174-175)] and clauses.

* Morphology:
(ساحتهم): a name for an open field or an open stretch of ground; its wazn is فعلة (with fatḥa and sukūn).

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «فإذا نزل بساحتهم».
In the pronoun there is an implicit metaphor. The punishment is likened to an army that suddenly attacks a people in their homes and descends upon them; "descending" is the imaginative attribute (takhyīl).
2- The loose figurative expression (al-majāz al-mursal): in His saying, the Exalted, «فساء صباح المنذرين».
They often hear of the raid in the morning, since in most cases it occurs then. This is a majāz mursal in which time is mentioned and what occurred in it is meant, as one says: "the days of the Arabs" for their battles.

* Benefits:
- The prepositional حتّى:
حتى has many uses. Among its uses is that it comes as a preposition in the position of إلى in meaning and operation, as occurs in the verse we are dealing with فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى حِينٍ but it differs from it in three respects:
1- Its genitive noun has two conditions:
a- That it be an overt noun, not a pronoun.
b- That its genitive noun be something other (than the whole), as in (أكلت السمكة حتى رأسها) ("I ate the fish, even its head"), or adjoining the last part, as in (سَلامٌ هِيَ حَتَّى مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ).
2- When there is no indication with it requiring the inclusion of what follows it, as in the verse: ألقى الصحيفة كي يخفف رحله ... والزاد حتى نعله ألقاها (He threw away the scroll to lighten his load ... and the provisions, even his sandal, he threw away)
or its non-inclusion, as in the verse:
سقى الحيا الأرض حتى أمكن غريت ... لهم فلا زال عنها الخير مجدودا (The rain watered the earth until ... for them, so may good never cease to be cut off from it) [Translator's note: the second verse is translated as written; the word غريت is unclear in the source, and the gloss is approximate.]
His saying (لا زال عنها) is the indication that prevents what follows حتى from falling under the ruling of what precedes it, and in such a case, what follows إلى is judged as not included.
3- Each of the two may occur alone in a place unsuitable for the other.
Of what إلى alone allows: "كتبت إلى زيد وأنا لي عمرو", that is, "he is my goal", as in the hadith «أنابك وإليك», and سرت من البصرة إلى الكوفة, where one may not say حتى زيد, nor حتى عمرو, nor حتى الكوفة.
