The impermissibility of (حتى الكوفة) is due to the weakness of حتى in expressing the end-point, so they did not set it against the beginning-point.
Of what حتى alone allows is that an accusative imperfect verb may follow it, as in His saying, the Exalted, وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ where the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar made genitive by حتى. The Kufans differ, making the verb accusative by حتى itself, whereas حتى is specific to nouns and so does not govern verbs.

safi-cedvel:180-182.t:
* I'rab:
(سبحان ربّك) like سبحان الله «1»; (ربّ) a badal from ربّك, genitive; (عمّا يصفون): its i'rab has already been given «2».
The clause « (نسبّح) سبحان ربّك» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يصفون..» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-type - or noun-type - relative. (181) (الواو) a conjunction; (سلام) a mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: it begins with an indefinite noun because the expression denotes generality, so it is praise or supplication.]; (على المرسلين) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ سلام.
The clause «سلام على المرسلين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one.
(182) (الواو) a conjunction; (لله) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الحمد; (ربّ) a naʿt of the Majestic Name, genitive like it.
The clause «الحمد لله ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one.

safi-cedvel:87-87.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction. (ما) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being (ظنّكم). (بربّ) attached to the maṣdar ظنّكم.
The clause ... is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause «تعبدون» [Note: in verse (85) of this sūra.].

safi-cedvel:88-94.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction. (نظرة) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative. (في النجوم) attached to (نظر), by the verb's being given the sense of "reflected".
The clause «نظر ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumptive, that is: His people said, "Come out with us", and he looked ....
(89) (الفاء) conjunction in the six following places. The clause «قال ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نظر.
The clause «إنّي سقيم..» is in the position of an accusative, reported speech.
(90) - (تولّوا) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two silent letters.. and the (wāw) is the agent. (عنه) attached to (تولّوا). (مدبرين) an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) confirming the verb, and its sign of accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «تولّوا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause قال.
(91) - (إلى آلهتهم) attached to (راغ). (ألا) a particle of offering ...
The clause «راغ ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause تولّوا.
The clause «قال..» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause راغ.
The clause «ألا تأكلون» is in the position of an accusative, reported speech.
(92) - (ما) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. (لكم) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما). (لا) negative.
The clause «ما لكم ... » has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «لا تأكلون» is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun of address in (لكم).
(93) (عليهم) attached to (راغ), and in "striking" there is the sense of rising over. (ضربا) mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb [Note: and the clause of the implied verb is a ḥāl from the agent of راغ.. or it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl.]. (باليمين) attached to the maṣdar (ضربا) [Note: This is if (ضربا) stands in for its verb; otherwise the prepositional phrase is attached to the implied verb.. The bāʾ may be one of accompaniment if اليمين means "strength", in which case the prepositional phrase is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of راغ.].
The clause «راغ (الثانية» ... has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause قال.
(94) (إليه) attached to (أقبلوا) - or to (يزفّون) - The clause «أقبلوا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied element, that is: he smashed them, and whoever saw him informed his people, and they came ...
The clause «يزفّون....» is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of أقبلوا.

* Morphology:
(راغ) contains a change by substitution: its origin is روغ; the wāw received a vowel after a fatḥa and was turned into alif. Its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas, meaning "he inclined to it secretly".
(نظرة) a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar marra) from the triliteral نظر; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa and sukūn.
(سقيم) a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral سقم, of the chapter fariḥa; its pattern is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
The art of symbolism, allusion and indirect hint: in His saying, the Exalted, «فَقالَ إِنِّي سَقِيمٌ».
This art is that the speaker wishes to conceal a matter in his speech and so places a symbol within it, either to obscure it for the addressee, to clear himself and to be free of blame, or so that through it one may be guided to the way of extracting what he concealed in his speech. What Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, said is an oblique expression, and by it he intended that whoever has death at his neck is sick. Of this is the proverb: "Health is enough of a disease."

* Benefits:
- The story of the stars:
What is the relation between Ibrāhīm's (peace and blessings be upon him) looking at the stars and his saying (إِنِّي سَقِيمٌ)?
The commentators said, and it is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās: The people of Ibrāhīm used to practise astrology, so he dealt with them in the way they practised and dealt, lest they reject him; for he wished to outwit them concerning their idols, so as to bind them with the argument that these are not to be worshipped. They had the next day a festival and gathering, and they used to go in to their idols and offer them sacrifices and set food before them before going out to their festival, claiming to seek blessing through it; when they returned from their festival they ate it. They said to Ibrāhīm: "Will you not come out with us?" So he looked at the stars and said, "I am sick", and while they were absent he proceeded to smash the idols.

[Translator's note: this line is a verbatim repetition of the السعي entry, attached in the source to الجبين; it is translated as written.]

(107) ذبح: a name for what is slaughtered, meaning the slaughtered animal; its pattern is فعل with kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Concision (ījāz): in His saying, the Exalted, «فَبَشَّرْناهُ بِغُلامٍ حَلِيمٍ».
This is ījāz qaṣr (concision by condensation), for this brief good news encompassed three things: that the child is a boy, a male; that he will reach the age of forbearance (ḥulm); and that he will be forbearing (ḥalīm).

* Benefits:
Who is the one to be sacrificed?
The verse indicated that the dreams of the prophets are true. The scholars differed over which of the two sons of Ibrāhīm was the one to be sacrificed. One group of them said he is "Isḥāq", and that is the view of ʿUmar, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, al-ʿAbbās, Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and others, may Allah be pleased with them. The reports from Ibn ʿAbbās differ in two sayings: one is Ismāʿīl and the other Isḥāq. Those who said it was Isḥāq said: This story took place in Shaʾm. It is reported from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he said: Ibrāhīm saw in a dream the slaughter of Isḥāq while he was in Shaʾm, so he travelled with him a journey of a month in one morning, until he brought him to the place of slaughter at Minā; when Allah ordered him to slaughter the ram, he slaughtered it, and travelled back with him a journey of a month in one evening journey, the valleys and mountains being folded up for him. The second saying: that it was Ismāʿīl, and that is the view of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, al-Shaʿbī, Mujāhid, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, al-Kalbī, and a report of ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ and Yūsuf ibn Māhak from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said the one ransomed was Ismāʿīl; and both sayings are reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Those who held that the sacrifice was Isḥāq argued from His saying, the Exalted, فَبَشَّرْناهُ بِغُلامٍ حَلِيمٍ فلما بلغ معه السعي: he was commanded to slaughter the one he had been given good news of, and nowhere in the Qur'an is it said that he was given good news of a child other than Isḥāq, and the good news came after the story of the sacrifice, which shows that the one to be sacrificed is the one given the good news. Those who held that the one to be sacrificed was Ismāʿīl argued that Allah the Exalted mentioned the good news of Isḥāq after finishing the story of the one to be sacrificed, saying, the Exalted, وَبَشَّرْناهُ بِإِسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ, which shows that the one slaughtered was other than him; and also that Allah the Exalted said in Sūrat Hūd فَبَشَّرْناها بِإِسْحاقَ وَمِنْ وَراءِ إِسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ, so how would He command him to slaughter Isḥāq when He had promised him a child by him, namely Yaʿqūb? And Ismāʿīl was described with patience, not Isḥāq, in His saying: وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ, which is his patience over the slaughter; and he was described with truthfulness to a promise in His saying إِنَّهُ كانَ صادِقَ الْوَعْدِ, for he promised his father to be patient over the slaughter and fulfilled his promise. ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz asked a Jew who had become Muslim and whose Islam was good: "Which of the two sons of Ibrāhīm did Allah the Exalted command him to slaughter?" He said: "Ismāʿīl." Al-Aṣmaʿī said: I asked Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ about the one to be sacrificed, and he said: "O Aṣmaʿī, when was Isḥāq ever in Mecca? It was only Ismāʿīl, and he is the one who built the House with his father." And Allah the Exalted knows best.
